chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Tunes lifted by others, and how many songs he composed
summary: Others sometimes added bars to his melodies and took credit; he estimates 35 or 40 compositions placed with publishers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. Have you ever -- this just comes to my mind -- have you ever had a -- written a song or a piece and somehow it became transferred to somebody else, and that person published it under their own name, has that
ever happened to you that you know of? You know, you hear a record someplace or you hear somebody playing something, you suddenly realize that's your song?

Oh, I've listened sometimes to something that sounds quite familiar to me, you know, especially about eight bars of certain things, you know, that you know you thought up, and some guys just put a few more bars with it, you know. They got the credit for the title and all that. Yes, those things have happened.
Uh-huh. Do you have any idea how many songs you have published -- had -- your own compositions I'm talking about, not arrangements, but compositions?
Compositions -- that's a good question, Tom. Let's see. I imagine 35 or 40, roughly, I would say, tunes that I had some dealings with, you know, with the publishers, the companies.
